newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy inflation falls to 27-year low.
newsitem.headline: Italy inflation falls to 27-year low.

text.p: Italian inflation fell to 2.6 percent year-on-year from 3.0 percent in October, its lowest level for 27 years, the national statistics office said on Thursday.
The consumer price index data, the lowest since June 1969 when inflation was 2.5 percent, was exactly in line with market forecasts and likely to fuel hopes for a swift interest rate cut.
The national statistics office ISTAT said in a statement that monthly CPI index rose 0.3 percent in November, compared with a rise of 0.1 percent in October and 0.6 percent in November 1995.
Year-on-year inflation was 6.0 percent in November last year.
Italian financial markets have been hoping for another cut in the key discount rate following October's 75 basis point cut to 7.5 percent.
Analysts polled before the inflation data said they expected the Bank of Italy to lower the rate by a further 50 basis points in early December.
